findings.finding: On 24 Sep 2026 the Delaware Supreme Court (Gendreau v. Movora, No. 447, 2025) affirmed the founder-seller's indemnity liability for the VOI/DePuy USD 70m settlement and REVERSED the two cuts the trial court had made against Vimian: the USD 9.8m license cost and half of the patent-litigation fees (about USD 4.3m). It reversed only the prejudgment interest on loan interest, and remanded. At the founder's roughly 55.6% share, that is about USD 8.5m of extra principal, on top of a USD 6.2m remainder Vimian carries at zero as doubtful. It also removes the appeal tail in which the USD 31.9m already collected could have been at risk. Vimian issued no release on it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The trial-court award (inside information, 30 Aug 2025 01:03) is the only precedent; the baseline has no clean reaction for it. A one-off with no path to the guide, so sized at a fraction: roughly EUR 12m of possible gain is about 0.65% of a market cap near EUR 1.85bn (530m shares x SEK 38.2), before collection and remand risk.
findings.why_not_priced: Vimian put no release on the Nasdaq feed between 21 Sep and 12 Oct, and Swedish searches (placera, borskollen) return only the 2025 trial-court award. Q2's note still said 'Judgment is expected no later than September'. If priced, there would have been a move around 24-25 Sep; the tape reads 35.35 -> 35.60, flat.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 report note on the litigation (amounts received, USD 6.2m remainder unrecorded): https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/a322053b30eb0829a4c35b575e792ab33

findings.finding: Specialty Pharma (about 44% of Q3 2025 revenue) laps a tough comparison. Q3 2025 SP organic growth was 11% including a US Specialised Nutrition retail campaign and 5% excluding it, and the 2026 campaign ran in Q2. So Q3 2026 SP organic growth works out mechanically at about 3-6% even if the underlying 9% holds. With MedTech about 10%, Vet Services 10% and Diagnostics 7%, my build gives group organic growth of about 6.5-7% against the 7.58% consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Organic growth is the line this name trades on: Q2 2025 (organic 5%, soft MedTech) fell 13.8% on the day; Q2 2026 beat organic (12%) and revenue (121.6 against 117) and rose only 3.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The company itself flagged the campaign timing, and consensus organic growth of 7.58% is already below Q2's 12%. The residual is only that a segment build lands about 0.5-1pp below the consensus. If fully priced, consensus would read about 6.5-7%.

findings.finding: The controlling owner, Fidelio Capital (closely associated with board member Gabriel Fitzgerald), bought 4,163,955 shares at SEK 34.90 on 21 Aug and a further 7,094,240 shares at about SEK 33.7-34.4 on 9-16 Sep 2026: about 11.3m shares, roughly SEK 390m and 2.1% of the company. The last purchase came days before the 30-day MAR closed period ahead of the 22 Oct report, and a board-affiliated buyer cannot trade on inside information, so no material adverse Q3 deviation was known by mid-September.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fidelio also bought SEK 62m in June 2026 ahead of the Q2 print, which rose 3.7%. The stock is up from about 34.5 to 38.1 since the September purchases.

findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Finwire reported every purchase in Swedish and the stock is up about 10% since, which matches the +7% 20-day run-up and the +0.63 lean. What remains is the read-through on the quarter, which the market may underweight on a 40% free float. If fully priced, the September volume spikes would have been followed by no drift; instead the stock kept climbing in mid-October.

findings.finding: Peer read-through: Virbac reported Q3 2026 sales on 19 Oct of EUR 400m, +8.8% at constant scope and FX. Companion animals rose 8.8% and North America 9.5% organically, against a TP ICAP Midcap estimate of EUR 384m, and Virbac now targets the top of its 5.5-7.5% growth range. Companion-animal demand held through the quarter Vimian is reporting.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no measured Vimian reaction to Virbac prints. Vimian rose 35.0 -> 38.25 over 8-16 Oct, before Virbac, and was flat on 20-21 Oct after it.
findings.original_quote: Virbac vise le haut de la fourchette de ses objectifs (French: 'Virbac targets the top of its objectives range'); T3 +8,8% à taux de change et périmètre constants
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer proxy, and Vimian's niches (specialised nutrition, orthopaedic and dental implants, vet clinic services) are not Virbac's mix. The flat tape on 20-21 Oct suggests no one traded the read-through, but this is a proxy, kept small.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 operating cash flow was EUR 3.8m (22.2) on a EUR 21.3m net working capital build, taking NWC to 26% of revenue from 21%. The company blamed receivables after a strong finish to the quarter, tax payments AND higher inventory. Q3 cash conversion is therefore a line the release will carry that the market has not seen.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Q2's weak cash flow the stock still rose 3.7%; Q4 2025's strong cash (55.7m) came with a +11.1% day.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus previews cover only P&L lines (the Modular table has no cash flow line), so a second weak cash quarter would be new. The sign is uncertain because the company called most of it timing, so the size is small.
